text:
Predicates:
Engaged(x) ::: x is engaged.
MakeWeddingPlans(x) ::: x makes wedding plans.
Invite(x, y) ::: x invites y to their ceremony.
Wedding(x) ::: x is a wedding.
WellAttended(x) ::: x has a well-attended wedding.
LargerFamily(x) ::: x has a larger family.
John ::: John (constant)
Premises:
∀x (MakeWeddingPlans(x) → Engaged(x)) ::: All people who make wedding plans are engaged.
∀x (Invite(x, y) → MakeWeddingPlans(x)) ::: All people who invite others to their ceremony make wedding plans.
∀x (Wedding(x) ∧ WellAttended(x) → Invite(x, y)) ::: Anyone who has a well-attended wedding invites others to come to their ceremony.
∃x (Wedding(x) ∧ LargerFamily(x)) → ∃x (Wedding(x) ∧ LargerFamily(x)) ::: Some people that have well-attended weddings have larger families.
Engaged(John) → (¬Invite(John, y) ∧ MakeWeddingPlans(John)) ::: If John is engaged, then John does not invite friends to their ceremony and makes wedding plans.
LargerFamily(John) → (Wedding(John) ∨ Invite(John, y)) ::: If John has a larger family, then either John has a well-attended wedding or invites friends to their ceremony.
Conclusion:
¬LargerFamily(John) ::: John does not have a larger family.
